   Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                            2/16

1.​ General Regulations
     1.1.​ Weight Limit
There are no weight categories in group battles.

     1.2.​ List Requirements
Fights of the Buhurt International group battles category are conducted in the list with a hard surface and
a rail. Depending on the type of the tournament, the size of the list may vary, provided it was agreed with
Buhurt International and documented in the tournament Regulations.

          1.2.1.​   Dimensions
●​           3v3: Length: 7 to 20 m | Width: 5 to 15 m
●​           5v5: Length: 9 to 20 m | Width: 7 to 15 m
●​           12v12: Length: 15 to 20 m | Width: 7 to 15 m
●​           30v30: Length: 25 to 30 m | Width: 12.5 to 20 m


          1.2.2.​   List Height
The height of the rail is 0.9 to 1.3 m.

          1.2.3.​   Safe Zone
An organizer must provide a fenced, 2m wide safety zone around every side of the list.

          1.2.4.​   Table Top Size
The table top width should be between 50 - 70 cm.

     1.3.​ Roles Allowed in the Safe Zone
     ●​    Marshals,
     ●​    Team support (Handing over reserve weapons) in designated areas within the safe zone,
     ●​    Team manager (Captain, Coach) in designated areas within the safe zone,
     ●​    Secretaries,
     ●​    Technical staff (List maintenance),
     ●​    Media (Only approved media staff).

Accessing the safe zone without a designated role above may result in a penalty (yellow card) for the
individual or team.
Of the above roles, only marshal teams are allowed to rest their hands on top of the list; this may result
in a penalty.




     Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                     3/16

2.​ Marshals Committee
The Marshals Committee of a tournament should consist of:

  2.1.​ The Knight Marshal (Chief Official)
 ●​ Is appointed by the Tournament Organizer.
 ●​ Shall make the final decision in the case of any disagreement.
 ●​ Supervises the course of the fight and assesses the team’s interactions.
 ●​ Can return a fighter who was grounded by unauthorized technique to the fight, or withdraw the
    fighter who is ‘out of battle’.
 ●​ Shall break inactive clinches with the “Break” local command and a yellow flag between the
    helmets of the fighters. The fighters must stop fighting immediately and take two steps apart.
 ●​ Shall stop rounds with the “Hold” command and yellow flag between helmets of the fighters. The
    fighters must stop across the entire list and should not move.
 ●​ Is the only one allowed to use the command “Start fight” and a signal with a flag that will start the
    round.
 ●​ Is the only one allowed to use the command “Stop fight” and a signal with a flag that will stop the
    round.
 ●​ Is the only one allowed to use the command “All rise” verbally.


  2.2.​ Field Marshals
 ●​ Shall break inactive clinches with the “Break” local command and a yellow flag between the
    helmets of the fighters. The fighters must stop fighting immediately and take two steps apart.
     Local command “Fight” and a signal with a flag of the same marshal who announced the break
     indicates the recommencement of the fight for the fighters pulled out of the clinch, and a
     continuation of the fight in general.
     Local commands “Break” and “Fight” are effective only for the fighters in the clinch. After the “Fight”
     command, any fighter can continue the fight with the same opponent or attack another opponent.
 ●​ Will stop a fight on the command of the Knight Marshal “Stop fight” the field marshals will stop the
    fight with verbal commands and a yellow flag.


  2.3.​ Line Marshals
There are between 4 and 8 Line Marshals.
 ●​ They are the external eyes of the Knight Marshal and Field Marshals in Buhurt.
 ●​ They look for and report rules violations, armour malfunctions and any other situation in the list to
    the Knight Marshal or Field Marshal during the fight.
 ●​ Particular Line Marshals will keep watch of the allocated weapon distribution zone and inform the
    Knight Marshal or Field Marshals of any rule’s violation.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                         4/16

●​ A line marshal may only interfere with the fight under the following circumstances:
      ○​ By direct order of the Knight Marshal.
      ○​ To prevent a direct threat to a competitor’s safety.
      ○​ To break an inactive clinch.
 ●​ After the round, the Line Marshal is to report any relevant information to the Knight Marshal.


  2.4.​ The Secretary
 ●​ Shall document the course and results of fights.
 ●​ Shall compile the tournament ladders, and determine the winner of the group stage based on
    registered results of the individual fights.
 ●​ For the countries/regions with a certification system in place, a secretary must hold a certificate
    issued by a local/regional/international Tournament committee.


  2.5.​ The Authenticity Committee Representative (AC rep)


  2.6.​ Number of Marshals
The number of marshals is determined separately for each tournament, depending on its form.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                         5/16

3.​ Team Structure
  3.1.​ Composition
Teams participating in group battles consist of the following members:
  ●​ Team Manager (captain, coach)
  ●​ Team Support
  ●​ Competitors


  3.2.​ Competitors
Competitors cannot be on multiple teams in a single category at a tournament.
Once the tournament has started, team rosters are locked in and can not be changed.
Teams may replace competitors from their tournament roster in any frequency and number between the
rounds or matches.


  3.3.​ Number of Reserve Competitors and Support in the Safety Zone
Competitors can have a team manager or support role.
 ●​ 3v3 Team: 5 competitors,1 team manager, 1 support
 ●​ 5v5 Team: 8 competitors, 1 team manager, 1 support
 ●​ 12v12 Team: 20 competitors, 1 team manager, 2 supports
 ●​ 30v30 Team: 50 competitors, 1 team manager, 3 supports

During the Matches the competitors are not allowed in the safety zone (see section 1.3 above).


  3.4.​ Alternative Composition
Organizers decide on the team composition for other types of group battles.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                     6/16

4.​ Match Structure

  4.1.​ Match and Round Win Criteria
A match is won when a team secures victory in 2 rounds before the opposing team.
A round is stopped when a team is outnumbered by a ratio of 3 to 1, with a round victory going to the
outnumbering team.
Each fighter still standing will be recorded in the scoresheet.
     Examples:
     3 vs 1 : stop fight and record “3-1”
     6 vs 2 : stop fight and record “6-2”
     3 vs 2 : continue the fight

  4.2.​ Group Stage
Time Limit for Each Match: 10 minutes.
Time Limit for Each Round: 5 minutes.
If the time limit is reached, the team with the most active (not grounded) competitors wins.
If the match ends in a draw (provided the number of round victories was a draw), record the match as a
draw.


  4.3.​ Round Robin, Elimination Brackets, Semi-finals, and Finals
A match cannot end in a draw.
Time Limit for Each Match: Unlimited.
Time Limit for Each Round: 5 minutes.
If the time limit is reached, the team with the most active (not grounded) competitors wins.

    4.3.1.​   Resolving a Draw in a match

  ●​ Initial Rounds
        ○​ If no team wins two rounds after the first two rounds, a third round is fought.

  ●​ Third Round
        ○​ During the third round:
        ○​ If both teams have only one competitor left standing, the fight stops upon a
           'Hold' command.
        ○​ The timer is paused.
        ○​ Competitors are led to the middle of the list. Then initiate the Champions Fight
        ○​ A winner is determined according to the rules of the ‘Champion’s Fight’.
        ○​ If the third round ends in a draw, a fourth round is fought.

  ●​ Fourth Round
        ○​ During the fourth round:
        ○​ If both teams have only one competitor left standing, the fight stops upon a
           'Hold' command.


  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                    7/16

○​    The timer is paused.
        ○​    Competitors are led to the middle of the list. Then initiate the Champions Fight
        ○​    A winner is determined according to the rules of the ‘Champion’s Fight’.
        ○​    If the fourth round ends in a draw, a fifth round is fought.

  ●​ Fifth Round
        ○​ The rules of the 'Champion’s Fight' are applied.
        ○​ Teams are allowed to select a competitor to represent them in this final round.
        ○​ If the fifth round ends at a draw, repeat this process.


  4.4.​ Champion's Fight Rules
The Champion's Fight follows the general rules for group fights with specific adjustments and limitations.

    4.4.1.​    General Setup
The fight begins with both competitors positioned in the middle of the list.

    4.4.2.​    Time Limit
There is no time limit for the Champion's Fight. The fight continues until a winner is determined.

    4.4.3.​    Prohibited Actions
It is strictly prohibited to touch the barrier of the list with any part of the body, including:
   ●​ Extremities (arms, hands, legs, feet),
   ●​ Head,
   ●​ Shield.

A competitor who touches the barrier of the list with any of these parts is immediately declared the
loser of the fight.

    4.4.4.​    Permitted Actions
Weapons are allowed to make contact with the barrier of the list during the fight.

    4.4.5.​    Victory Conditions
A competitor loses the fight if:
  ●​ They touch the barrier of the list as described above.
  ●​ They are otherwise defeated according to the rules of group fights.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                         8/16

5.​ Fight Procedure
  5.1.​ Before the fights

       5.1.1.​   Weapon and Shields Check
A weapon check is conducted by Marshals and Authenticity Rep before the fights for every tournament.
All weapons and shields are to be checked to ensure their safety and authenticity compliance.
Only weapons and shields marked as approved during this check are allowed in the list and as reserve
weapons handed by teams’ supports.

       5.1.2.​   Authenticity and Safety Check
Depending on the rank of the tournament, every fighter of each team has to undergo an Authenticity
check of their armor before entering the list.
This check will be conducted by an Authenticity Rep.
A marshal can also be part of this check, to ensure the safety aspect of the armor (example: a check of
the neck protection).


  5.2.​ Entering the list

       5.2.1.​   Team Invitation and Preparation
The Knight Marshal (either directly or via the Secretary) invites the 2 teams to the list and announces
their preparation.

The two invited teams must report to the designated area next to the list for Invited teams are
expected to report to the list within 1 minute.

If a team fails to report to the list within 3 minutes, their opponent is awarded a technical win of the
match or the fight starts with an uneven number of competitors (example: 5-4, 5-3…).

       5.2.2.​   Identity Verification
The Knight Marshal can request competitors to enter the list with their helmets off.
Once the competitors identities are verified:
  ●​ They are given 90 seconds to put on their helmets and prepare for the fight.
  ●​ Support outside of the list may assist competitors during this preparation phase.
Competitors are not allowed to leave the list before the start of the fight. This measure ensures that no
unregistered competitors are fielded by the team.

       5.2.3.​   Line up
The competitors enter the list prepared for the match and form a line for the marshal check.

  ●​    5v5: Competitors form a single line.
  ●​    12v12: competitors form 2 rows of 6 competitors, keeping column alignment
  ●​    30v30: competitors form 3 rows of 10 competitors, keeping column alignment.
  ●​    The formations for other types of fights must be documented in the Tournament Regulations or
        determined by the Knight Marshal.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                      9/16

Everyone, except for the Knight Marshal, field marshals, competitors, and a Team Manager (captain,
coach), leaves the list.
The Team Manager (captain, coach) counts their competitors and reports readiness to the Knight
Marshal.
The Knight Marshal checks the number of competitors on each team.

       5.2.4.​   Marshal Check
Once positioned in the line up (or at the gate entrance, depending on the tournament organization) each
fighter will be submitted to a marshal check.
Will be verified:
  ●​    the approval mark on their weapons/shields,
  ●​    the strap securing their helmets,
  ●​    the protection of their neck,
  ●​    any other safety element marshals wish to verify.

   5.3.​ Starting the fight
Team Managers (captains, coaches) leave the list.
Field Marshals take positions behind the teams’ formations near the gates.
The Knight Marshal requests field marshals to signal readiness and absence of unauthorized
participants in the list.
The Knight Marshal commands:
  ●​ “Team ready”: Teams can then assume their positions.
  ●​ “Fight“, accompanied by a flag signal: fight begins.

   5.4.​ During the fight

       5.4.1.​   Grounding a Competitor
Both the Knight Marshal and Field marshals can ground a competitor from the list in the following cases:
  ●​ Multiple verbal warnings being ignored in a round.
  ●​ Multiple Prohibited Fighting Techniques or Other Prohibited Actions.
  ●​ Grounding your opponent by an illegal action where your opponent is unable to immediately rejoin
     the round.
  ●​ Being grounded does not replace other penalties (e.g., yellow or red cards)

Grounded competitors must remain on the ground until the Knight Marshal commands “All Rise.”
After the “All Rise” command, teams return to their initial positions.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                     10/16

5.4.2.​   Removing Competitor from the list
Both the Knight Marshal and field marshals must withdraw a competitor from the list in the following
cases:

  ●​ A competitor continues offensive actions after being grounded.
  ●​ A competitor loses their helmet.
  ●​ A Knight marshal can remove a competitor if they deem necessary.

  5.5.​ End of the round or fight
A round is finished only after the Knight Marshal’s command of "Stop fight!"

Marshals report any rules violations to the Knight Marshal.

The Knight Marshal can, based on these reports and personal observations:

  ●​    Decide the result.
  ●​    Processes appeals.
  ●​    Announce the score of the round or fight.
  ●​    Imposes warnings, yellow cards, or red cards.

After the end of the round or fight, the Knight Marshal can:

  ●​ Declare the round finished and announce the score.
  ●​ Announce a rematch with full or differentiated teams (e.g., 2v3, 3v4, 4v4, 4v5) if deemed
     necessary.

  5.6.​ Forfeit procedure
A team manager (captain, coach) can throw a white flag “forfeit" to signal the Knight Marshal to stop the
fight.
In such cases:
  ●​ The opponents are awarded a technical win.
  ●​ The number of active competitors in the list is recorded as 5-0.

The first white flag results in a round loss.
The second white flag results in a match loss.
After the third white flag, the team is withdrawn from the tournament.


  5.7.​ Record Keeping
The secretary records the results. At the end of the round, the secretary registers:
 ●​ The round win.
 ●​ The round score (number of active competitors of the both teams at the end of the round).
 ●​ The time of the round.
 ●​ The warnings, cards and appeals




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                      11/16

6.​ Penalties
  6.1.​ Verbal Warning
A verbal warning is imposed for insignificant rule violations and serves to indicate the violation to the
competitor.
The verbal warning is recorded on the scoresheet with the following info:
  ●​ belt flag number of the competitor,
  ●​ name of the competitor,
  ●​ description of the warning.

A verbal warning can’t affect scoring.


  6.2.​ Warning (Yellow Card)
A yellow card is recorded on the scoresheet with the following info:
  ●​ belt flag number of the competitor,
  ●​ name of the competitor,
  ●​ description of the card.

A yellow card can affect the scoring.

    6.2.1.​   Reasons for Receiving a Yellow Card

  ●​ The competitor delivered a prohibited action listed in the “Buhurt Rules” document.
  ●​ The competitor performed an action not listed in the Authorized Fighting Techniques section
     listed in the “Buhurt Rules” document.
  ●​ The competitor got to their feet from being grounded before the command “All Rise.”
  ●​ The competitor started the fight before the “Fight” command.
  ●​ The competitor conducted offensive actions after the “Stop Fight” command and while the yellow
     flag was hung in front of their helmet.
  ●​ The competitor purposely ignored a marshal’s command.
  ●​ The competitor continued to fight while aware that they had lost a significant element of their
     armor.

    6.2.2.​   Double Yellow Card
Depending on the severity of the violation, the Knight Marshal may impose 1 or 2 yellow cards for these
actions.
A competitor who receives 2 yellow cards is disqualified.
Two yellow cards are equivalent to one red card.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                     12/16

6.3.​ Disqualification (Red Card)
A red card is imposed for severe rule violations or as a result of receiving a second yellow card.
The red card is recorded on the scoresheet with the following info:
  ●​ belt flag number of the competitor,
  ●​ name of the competitor,
  ●​ description of the card.

A red card can affect scoring.
A competitor who receives a red card is withdrawn from the tournament.

    6.3.1.​   Reasons for Disqualification
  ●​ Systematic rule violations (e.g., 2 yellow cards during the tournament).
  ●​ Injuring an opponent with an unauthorized action, resulting in the opponent's inability to continue
     participating in the tournament (requires confirmation by a medic).
  ●​ Harsh and systematic arguments with marshals, groundless challenging of decisions, or
     rude/derogatory behavior toward opponents or participants.

    6.3.2.​   Injury Clause

If an injured competitor continues competing and claims injury later in the tournament, this will not lead to
a red card. If the injured competitor participates in any category, the red card will be downgraded, and
the Judiciary Committee will investigate and penalties may apply.
If a competitor continues to fight in rounds after receiving an illegal hit but later withdraws due to an
“injury” claimed to be from the illegal hit, this does not result in an upgrade to a red card.

    6.3.3.​   Red Card Consequences for the Team line up

When a competitor is disqualified, their team fields one less competitor than their opposition (but no
fewer than 3 competitors) for:
  ●​ The match during which the disqualification was imposed.
  ●​ The next match in the tournament.

       Example:
If the opposition cannot meet the required number of competitors (e.g., 12 in 12v12), the penalized team
will be placed in a disadvantageous position. If both teams receive red cards, neither gains an
advantage.

  6.4.​ Infraction in Authenticity Rules (Green Card)
An official authenticity warning (green card) is a penalty imposed for an authenticity rule violation that is
registered in the protocol of the tournament, and affects the competitor’s rating. A green card combined
with a yellow card result in a red card, and the fighter is disqualified.

The competitor can receive one 1 green card only once they choose to enter the list with the appropriate
infraction level based upon the Infraction classification document.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                         13/16

6.5.​ Team Disqualification
A team may be disqualified under the following circumstances:

    6.5.1.​   Exceeding the permitted number of competitors
In such cases, their opposition is automatically awarded the victory.
If this rule violation is detected after the fact, the violating team’s results are annulled.
If detected during finals, trophies are withdrawn, and other competitors move up the ladder.

    6.5.2.​   Card limit
The team competitors, manager and/or support receive a combination of card as followed:
  ●​ Two red cards and one yellow card.
  ●​ Any variation totaling 5 yellow cards (red cards count as two yellow cards).
This applies only to the category being competed in.
Green cards do not count in team disqualification.

    6.5.3.​   Harassment or Systematic Arguing
If a competitor, a team manager or a team support engages in:
  ●​ Harsh and systematic arguments with marshals.
  ●​ Groundless challenges to decisions.
  ●​ Rude or derogatory behavior toward opponents or participants.

    6.5.4.​   A competitor entered the list after the competitors were counted


  6.6.​ Additional Notes on Cards
All cards are individual warnings and are observed by the Judiciary Committee.
Yellow cards received by a team manager (captain, coach) or support staff result in disciplinary
measures per general card regulations.
Cards are summed regardless of the person’s role (competitor, team manager, or support).​




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                    14/16

7.​ Appeal
  7.1.​ How to Appeal
The team captain or the captain’s representative may appeal a decision made by the Marshals’ Team
or the Knight Marshal.
Appeals are submitted to the Secretary.
The number of appeals is determined by the Tournament Organizer.
It is recommended to allow 1 appeal.
Important: If an appeal is approved, the competitor may submit an additional appeal.


  7.2.​ When to Appeal
The team captain or captain’s representative must announce their intention to appeal in person to the
Secretary.
Appeals must be submitted:
  ●​ Within 15 minutes after the end of the match.
  ●​ Before the start of the fights in the next phase of the competition.


  7.3.​ Why to Appeal
An appeal can be filed for the following reasons:
  ●​ False implementation of a penalty (reprimand, warning, or disqualification).
  ●​ Unregistered rule violations by the opponent that should result in a penalty (reprimand, warning,
     or disqualification).


  7.4.​ Result of the Appeal
The possible outcomes of an appeal could include:
  ●​ A general rematch of the round.
  ●​ Restart from a particular point.
  ●​ The imposition or withdrawal of yellow cards.
  7.5.​ Appeal to the Judiciary Committee
If the team captain is dissatisfied with the Knight Marshal’s decision, they may appeal to the Buhurt
International Judiciary Committee.




  Buhurt Regulations V. 26.4                                                                   15/16
